jobs.title: Head of Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Company Description
Uyir Lab is an AI research lab focused on making AI agents accurate in underrepresented languages, as they are truly spoken in everyday life. The lab addresses gaps in dialects, code-mixing, and cultural context for languages that are widely spoken but barely present on the web, starting with Tamil and expanding to Sinhala, Punjabi, Swahili, Hausa, Amharic, Fula, Oromo, Javanese, Bhojpuri, and more. Uyir Lab’s approach combines consented voice data from native speakers, deep linguistic mapping, and proprietary models like Nila for Tamil, delivered via a “Language Brain” layer that plugs into existing AI agents. As AI takes on critical work in sectors such as banking, health, and customer service, Uyir Lab’s mission is to reduce costly misunderstandings and give every language a life in AI, working closely with agent builders, native speakers, and community partners.
Role Description
The Head of Machine Learning is a full-time remote role leading the design, development, and deployment of language-focused ML systems across Uyir Lab’s growing portfolio of models and languages. This position oversees end-to-end machine learning pipelines: defining research directions, shaping model architectures, guiding experimentation, and driving productionization of models for real-world AI agents. The role includes managing and mentoring a multidisciplinary ML team, collaborating with data engineers and linguists to build high-quality datasets, and ensuring robust evaluation for dialect-aware, culturally grounded performance. The Head of Machine Learning partners with product and engineering teams to integrate Uyir Lab’s “Language Brain” into external applications, sets technical standards for scalability and reliability, and contributes to strategic decisions about new languages, platforms, and partnerships.
Qualifications

Strong foundations in Computer Science, including algorithms, data structures, distributed computing, and software engineering best practices.
Expertise in Machine Learning and Data Science, covering model development, training at scale, evaluation, optimization, and experimentation workflows.
Specialized experience in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for low-resource or multilingual settings, including sequence models, transformers, and representation learning.
Hands-on skills in Pattern Recognition, statistical modeling, and signal processing methods relevant to speech, text, and multimodal data.
Proficiency with modern ML ecosystems (e.g., Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, Hugging Face, ML Ops tools) and cloud-based training infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience leading ML or research teams, setting technical direction, and delivering production-ready models in collaboration with product and engineering.
Background in building or improving language technologies (ASR, MT, chatbots, dialogue systems, or language understanding) is highly beneficial.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology, Full-Time
jobs.description:
The Program

At Taproot Community Support Services, we’re a 100 percent employee-owned organization through an Employee Ownership Trust (EOT). Every employee is an owner from their first day, with a voice in shaping Taproot’s future and the opportunity to share in employee ownership dividends.

As a Certified B Corporation, we harness business for good. Since 1983 we’ve grown steadily, now delivering support across Alberta, British Columbia, and Ontario through more than 90 contracts.

Our 900-plus employee-owners live by five shared values: we are stronger together, we lead with optimism, we embrace challenges, we respect every voice, and we go above and beyond. Guided by these principles, we deliver more than 125 community-based services each year. We walk alongside about 1,600 children, youth, families, and people with diverse abilities, with revenues exceeding $70 million.

Our Support Office provides the systems, data and services that help our programs do their best work. As we grow, we are looking for a Director of Information Technology to lead our technology strategy, information systems and IT operations.

The Position

Help shape how technology powers a growing, employee-owned organization. As our Director of Information Technology, you’ll report to the Chief Operating Officer and work alongside senior leaders across three provinces to make our technology secure, connected and easy to use. You’ll lead the work that matters most: bringing case management onto one system, connecting our systems and data, building reporting leaders can rely on, strengthening SharePoint and digital records, and helping Taproot adopt AI thoughtfully and responsibly. You’ll lead a team of system administrators and a data analyst, partner with external IT providers, and see your work make a real difference for our staff and the people we serve.

Schedule

One (1) permanent, full-time position available, working 40 hours per week:

Hours, e.g. 0830-1630 Monday through Friday
Some travel is required.

In Your Role You Will

Manage / Oversee a Number Of Areas That Include

Strategy & Team Leadership

Develop and deliver an IT and digital strategy that aligns with organizational goals, and develop and manage the IT budget, including yearly licence and cloud cost reviews.
Lead and develop the IT team, including system administrators and a data analyst: setting clear priorities, assigning work, coaching, and supporting performance and growth.
Lead several cross-functional projects at once using structured project management, and lead change management with HR, Quality and programs to support successful adoption.

Systems, Data & AI

Oversee core systems, including Microsoft 365/SharePoint, ShareVision, Inclusion and iTacit, and lead system implementation, integration and data migration.
Lead SharePoint structure, permissions and governance, and support digital records management.
Oversee organizational reporting and dashboards in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, and set up data governance.
Optimize systems and workflows to reduce manual work, using automation and AI where it adds value, and lead the responsible adoption of AI, including Microsoft Copilot.

Infrastructure, Security & Support

Oversee the helpdesk and ticketing system, set and monitor service level agreements (SLAs), and report IT metrics to management.
Manage security and IT software, including endpoint detection and response (EDR) and antivirus, as well as backup, disaster recovery and business continuity planning.
Oversee IT hardware and asset management (laptops, desktops, cellphones and printers), including purchasing, tracking and lifecycle management.
Establish IT policies that safeguard our data and meet legal, privacy and accreditation requirements.

Vendors & Relationships

Manage IT and telecommunications vendors, and keep a central record of contracts, renewal dates and costs.
Represent Taproot at meetings and build positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Perform miscellaneous job-related duties as required.
A complete and detailed list of key responsibilities can be available at time of interview.
Prior to confirmation of employment, all applicants must provide a copy of a current Criminal Record Check and/or Government Screening Letter. These checks vary depending on province and sector and will be communicated by the Program Hiring Team.

As An Ideal Candidate You Possess

A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in IT management or a similar role, with a track record of leading successful projects, including a large system implementation or digital transformation.
Strong experience with Microsoft 365 and Azure, including SharePoint Online, and with system integration and data migration.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, and a solid understanding of data governance.
Hands-on experience rolling out generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot.
Strong knowledge of cyber security, risk management and compliance.
Excellent team leadership, project management and change management skills, with the ability to explain technology in plain language.
Project management certification, change management training, and experience in community social services or health care are assets.
Valid Class 5 Driver’s License and clean driver’s abstract.

What Taproot Community Support Services Does

At Taproot, your passion for helping others can truly make a difference. As an employee-owned company, we value collaboration, learning, and innovation. Our strength-based approach guides both our care and how we support each other. Join a team where your voice matters, and together, we're building a company we're proud of.

Our Employees Enjoy

Employee ownership from day one through our EOT, with opportunity for profit-sharing dividends
Work/life balance
Learning and career development opportunities
Competitive wages and salaries
Paid vacation and benefits for eligible employees
Defined benefit pension plan (Municipal Pension Plan) for eligible employees within British Columbia
Matching RRSP plan for eligible employees within Alberta
Professional development opportunities and job-related training
Employee and Family Assistance Program
Long Service Milestone rewards
Employee referral bonus program
A values-driven workplace — as a Certified B Corp, we're committed to using business as a force for good

For more information on Taproot Community Support Services visit our website: taproot.ca

No candidate will meet every single desired qualification. If your experience looks a little different from what we've identified and you think you can bring value to the role, we'd love to learn more about you! Please apply.

Equal-Opportunity Employer

Our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment is unwavering. We believe that varied backgrounds and experiences fuel innovation and success. As an equal-opportunity employer, we prioritize diversity, equity, and inclusion across all operations. We're seeking candidates passionate about contributing to our multicultural teams and enriching our workplace with their unique insights and cultural sensitivity.

We encourage individuals from diverse backgrounds to apply and join us in fostering a welcoming and inclusive environment.

No telephone calls please. Only those candidates selected for an interview will be notified.

jobs.description:
Director of Finance

Location:
Toronto, Ontario -onsite
Language:
Strong written and spoken English communication skills required
Employment Type:
Permanent, Full-Time

About the Opportunity

Are you a strategic finance leader who wants to make a meaningful impact? Our client, a well-established organization in the long-term care and non-profit sector, is seeking a Director of Finance
to join its Senior Leadership Team. This is an opportunity to shape financial strategy while supporting quality care and services for seniors.

Reporting to the CEO, you'll oversee financial operations, guide organizational planning, and collaborate with leadership, employees, and the Board of Directors. Your expertise will help strengthen financial sustainability and support a workplace where people come first.

What's in it for You

A purpose-driven environment where your work supports community well-being.
A collaborative leadership team that values thoughtful decision-making.
Opportunities to influence financial strategy and organizational growth.
Exposure to finance, human resources, governance, and long-term care operations.

Your Responsibilities

You'll lead financial operations, ensuring accurate reporting, strong financial controls, and regulatory compliance.
You'll oversee payroll, benefits, and financial administration for unionized and non-unionized employees.
You'll collaborate with the CEO, Board, and departmental leaders on budgeting, forecasting, audits, and financial planning.
You'll manage government funding requirements, charitable compliance, and financial reporting.
You'll provide oversight of HR administration, WSIB, return-to-work programs, and organizational risk management.
You'll enhance financial systems, policies, and processes to support operational efficiency.

Skills and Qualifications

5+ years of progressive financial administration experience, including senior-level responsibilities.
Professional accounting designation (CPA or recognized legacy designation).
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, budgeting, payroll, and regulatory compliance.
Experience in non-profit, healthcare, long-term care, or government-funded environments preferred.
Familiarity with Microsoft Great Plains and QHR payroll systems considered an asset.
Excellent leadership, communication, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.

Note from the Hiring Manager

"We're looking for a collaborative financial leader who understands that strong financial decisions help us deliver exceptional care and build a stronger organization."

Why Partner with Altis

If you’ve never worked with a staffing agency before, we make it easy. We work with top employers across Canada who have great jobs to fill, each vetted and verified by our team. When you apply for a job with Altis, we get to know you as a candidate and learn what your strengths are. Then, if you’re a solid match, we handle all the logistics, advocating for you as a candidate for the role, providing access to coaching and connecting you directly with the hiring manager. And rest assured, all our services are free of cost for candidates.
